caption: The clockless TNT engine with an on/off LEVER (vjeux 2026-10-21: "I thought we were going to remove the clock as we didn't need it"; "Can we have an on off switch for all the tnt"): tnt-triggered-launch-16b's engine, its holding redstone block replaced by a torch that holds the engine piston (lit while the lever is off) and the lever on the torch's stone; the obsidian under the piston is not needed. Lever off (as built): the torch holds the sticky piston extended, nothing moves. Lever on: the torch goes dark and the engine runs by itself, its frame's redstone block re-powering the piston through the dust every cycle: one TNT per 6 gt (200 TNT/min). Lever off again: the torch relights within 2 gt and the piston stays extended. It stands 6 blocks above the ground (stand: its safe drop over every kick: the TNT bursts under it).

PRECISE DROP with an on/off LEVER (vjeux 2026-10-21: "Can we have an on off switch for all the tnt"; coordinator: clean stop, nothing left in the channel). tnt-precise-drop's engine, P40 clock, water aligner and trapdoor, with two changes. (1) The release of each TNT no longer waits for the NEXT engine push (that stranded the last TNT in the water whenever the clock stopped): the engine's torch, relighting at each prime, fires a dropper into a ring of 11 hoppers whose comparator opens the trapdoor 53 gt later (one item per TNT, 4 items circling, 7 gt per hopper), so every TNT already has its release on the way when the machine stops. (2) The lever: a torch standing next to the clock's downward sticky piston holds it while the lever is off (the lever on the torch's stone turns the torch off). Lever off (as built): nothing moves, nothing primed. Lever on: the clock runs, one TNT per 40 gt (30 TNT/min), each at one point in mid-air 9.1 blocks under the machine. Lever off again: the clock stops within a cycle and the TNT still in the channel drops on time. Stands 23 blocks up (stand: the burst in mid-air, 13.9 blocks above the ground).

PRECISE AIR BURST with an on/off LEVER (vjeux 2026-10-21: "Can we have an on off switch for all the tnt"; coordinator: clean stop, nothing left on the launcher). tnt-airburst's engine, P54 clock, water channel and slime launcher, with two changes. (1) Each TNT's launch no longer waits for the NEXT engine push (a stop stranded the last TNT on the launcher): the engine's obsidian, powered by its dust each time the frame comes back (once per TNT), fires a dropper into a ring of 11 hoppers whose comparator, 63 gt after the prime, powers the launcher's repeater (5 items circling, 7 gt a hopper). (2) The lever: a torch on a wall behind the clock's downward sticky piston holds it while the lever is off (the lever under the torch's stone turns the torch off); built as the lever leaves it stopped (the clock's pistons extended, the engine piston extended). Lever off (as built): nothing moves, nothing primed. Lever on: one TNT per 54 gt (22.2 TNT/min), each launched up to one point in mid-air above the machine, which stands on the ground. Lever off: the clock stops within a cycle and the TNT on its way is still launched on time.

One TNT per BUTTON press (site QA 2026-10-21: a real button holds 20-30 gt, so the 16-block engine judged with a 4-tick removal of its holding redstone block lit several TNT per press). The engine of tnt-triggered-launch-16b with a one-shot hold instead: the obsidian beside the piston is strongly powered by a wall torch under it, which holds the piston; the torch hangs on the stone under the piston (in the obsidian foot's place) and the button is on that stone. A press powers the stone: the stone holds the piston itself and the torch goes dark. At the release the stone goes quiet 2 ticks before the torch relights: the piston drops, the frame comes back, its redstone block repowers the piston through the dust and the push lights ONE TNT, however long the press. Latency: the press, then 5 ticks.

Precise air burst, 44 blocks in a 5x5x10 box (250), 22.2 TNT/min: every lit TNT explodes at exactly the same point in the air, bit for bit, safe on the ground. clk-rt's minimum-volume search (explore/timer 37ee0ae37, designs/circuits/tracks/clk-rt/tnt-airburst-250-44b.txt): the 45-block 250-volume version with one block fewer. The 16b engine is held by a redstone torch that a 7-block catalog P54 clock darkens for one TNT per period; the TNT flies into fence posts over a water channel, the current pins it against a fence post standing on a slime block, and the next TNT's push, carried by observers, makes the sticky piston under the slime launch it straight up, so it explodes near the top of its flight, more than 7 blocks from anything a blast could break. material (clk-rt 2026-10-21, `circuit material`): 2 obsidian -> stone (the same kind, axis and metrics on its judge); obsidian at 5 1 -2 stays for immovability (pistons must not move it: the design fails or changes even with a blast-proof netherite block there); obsidian at 6 0 -7 stays for immovability (pistons must not move it: the design fails or changes even with a blast-proof netherite block there)

The TNT duper (vjeux 2026-10-20: one world-best implementation, built from catalog parts): 86 lit TNT a minute, standing right on the ground. Two catalog parts. The 16-block duplicator engine (tnt-triggered-launch-16b's, without its input block) makes one TNT each time its sticky piston loses power for a moment: held extended, released, it retracts, the redstone block on its slime frame comes back next to its dust and pushes it out again, which primes a TNT and throws it north at 1 block per tick. The clock is clk-obs-p14-lamp-obs-rb-stk-6b-b-0e0eb7 from the clock catalog (6 blocks, period 14 gt): its sticky piston moves a redstone block that sits next to the engine's piston (holding it) except for 4 ticks of every 14, so the engine dupes once per period. Each TNT lands and explodes on the ground 9 to 30 blocks away (7.4 to 27 on unbreakable ground), beyond the 6.9 blocks a blast can reach, so no explosion touches the machine and each one breaks ground blocks. Found by `mctas circuit tnt hold-scan` (every archived clock and turn, the cells where a piston is powered on all but one short window of the period, the engine's piston put there, judged on redsim); the 120-TNT-a-minute version (a period-10 clock) lands blasts as close as 5.3 blocks and failed 1 of 16 game builds in 3 of 6 runs. material (clk-rt 2026-10-21, `circuit material`): 1 obsidian -> stone (the same kind, axis and metrics on its judge); obsidian at 2 -1 2 stays for immovability (pistons must not move it: the design fails or changes even with a blast-proof netherite block there)

Precise drop, 41 blocks in a 6x5x8 box (240), 30 TNT/min: every TNT falls straight down from one point and explodes at one point in mid-air 10.0 blocks under the machine, 13.0 blocks above the ground it stands 23 blocks over. clk-rt's minimum-volume search (explore/timer 3670274e4, designs/circuits/tracks/clk-rt/tnt-precise-drop-240-41b.txt): the 240-volume version with 3 fewer blocks. A 7-block catalog P40 clock, folded between the engine and the channel, moves its redstone block in front of a repeater for 6 ticks every 40 and the torch under the engine piston goes dark: one TNT. The TNT flies into fence posts over a water channel, the current pins it against an observer on an iron trapdoor, and the next TNT's push, carried by observers and a delay-4 repeater, opens the trapdoor. material (clk-rt 2026-10-21, `circuit material`): 1 obsidian -> stone (the same kind, axis and metrics on its judge); obsidian at 5 -2 2 stays for immovability (pistons must not move it: the design fails or changes even with a blast-proof netherite block there)
